verifications.claim: Artemis II lunar flyby live coverage starts at 1 p.m. EDT on April 6, 2026, via NASA+, the NASA YouTube channel, and NASA's social media.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'A separate stream will start at 1 p.m. April 6 of the lunar flyby on NASA's YouTube channel.'; R3: 'live coverage ... on Monday, April 6, beginning at 1:00 p.m. ET ... NASA+, ... YouTube channel and social media accounts.'; R4: 'Coverage begins at 1 p.m. on NASA+, ... YouTube and the agency’s X account'; R5: '1 p.m. NASA’s live coverage ... on NASA+, ... YouTube channel.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact start time, date, and platforms including NASA+, YouTube, and social media.

verifications.claim: Coverage includes live views of the Moon from the Orion spacecraft on Netflix, Apple TV, Hulu, and Amazon Prime.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'streaming services ... hosting the NASA+ livestream ... including Netflix'; R4: 'Netflix ... will also host the NASA+ livestream'; R5: 'NASA’s live coverage ... on NASA+, Amazon Prime, Apple TV, Hulu, Netflix ... Coverage will include live views of the Moon from cameras mounted on Orion’s solar arrays.'
verifications.reasoning: R5 explicitly lists all platforms and confirms coverage includes live Moon views from Orion; others support specific platforms hosting NASA feed.

verifications.claim: NASA+ and YouTube provide continuous, comprehensive coverage starting at 1 p.m. EDT on April 6, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'livestream providing continuous coverage ... A separate stream will start at 1 p.m. April 6 ... on NASA's YouTube channel.'; R3: 'live coverage ... beginning at 1:00 p.m. ET ... NASA+, ... YouTube channel'; R5: '1 p.m. NASA’s live coverage ... on NASA+, ... 24/7 coverage on its YouTube channel.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm continuous/24/7 coverage on NASA+ and YouTube starting at 1 p.m. on the date.

verifications.claim: Netflix, Peacock, and other major platforms will host the NASA feed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'streaming services ... including Netflix and Peacock.'; R4: 'Netflix ... host the NASA+ livestream'; R5: 'Amazon Prime, Apple TV, Hulu, Netflix, HBO Max, and Roku.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly name Netflix, Peacock, and additional major platforms hosting NASA livestream.

verifications.claim: The Artemis Real-Time Orbit Website (AROW) is the official NASA tracker to monitor the spacecraft's position, speed, and distance.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '"Artemis Real-Time Orbit Website" (or AROW) ... see where the Orion spacecraft is, how fast it\'s traveling, and how many miles it is ... from both the Earth and the moon'; R4: 'Artemis II tracker ... see where Orion is, how fast it\'s traveling and how far the spacecraft is from both the Earth and the moon.'
verifications.reasoning: R2 names AROW explicitly as NASA's tracker for position, speed, distance; R4 describes identical functionality.

verifications.claim: AROW is available on desktop and as a mobile app.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'available on desktop and as a mobile app'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states AROW availability on desktop and mobile app.
